findings.issue: Third unguarded door into the state machine: a DRAFT can be promoted to «جديد» without a number. CorrespondenceStateMachine allows Draft → New (correctly, as the lifecycle table), and its own XML doc says the move happens "only through registration (incoming) or approval (outgoing) — the two operations that issue the official number", but ChangeStatusAsync (line 510) never checks the SOURCE state: after the Cancelled/Closed/Archived switch it goes straight to LoadAsync → EnsureTransition(Draft, New) → row.Status = New, issuing no number and calling neither OfficialNumberService nor the clock check. FollowUpService.AddAsync has the identical hole (statusTo = New on a draft). The resulting row is a permanent dead end: DeleteDraftAsync refuses it (Status != Draft), CancelAsync refuses it (OfficialNumber is null), CorrectionService refuses it (not numbered), UpdateDraftAsync still edits it freely, and meanwhile CorrespondenceStateMachine.IsOpen(New) is true so it is counted by AttentionService and the correspondence badge and can be moved to «بانتظار رد» and produce an unnumbered awaiting-reply card. This is exactly the class of bug round 2 fixed for Cancelled/Closed/Archived, left open for the one transition that issues the number. No test covers it: the only ChangeStatusAsync tests start from an already-registered row, and CorrespondenceStateMachineTests only asserts the pure table.
findings.fix: Refuse a Draft source at both public entry points rather than changing the transition table (the table is the correct documentation of the lifecycle). In CorrespondenceService.ChangeStatusAsync, immediately after `var row = await LoadAsync(...)` and before EnsureTransition, add: `if (row.Status == CorrespondenceStatus.Draft) { throw new CorrespondenceRefusedException(CoreAr.CorrRefusedDraftNeedsNumbering); }`. Add the same guard in FollowUpService.AddAsync inside the `if (statusTo is { } target)` block, beside the existing Cancelled/Closed/Archived refusal. Add one Arabic string to CoreAr beside CorrRefusedFollowupStatus, with no technical term and no error code, pointing at the command that does apply — e.g. `public const string CorrRefusedDraftNeedsNumbering = "المسودة تصبح جديدة بتسجيل الوارد أو اعتماد الصادر، وعندها يصدر رقمها";`. Tests: from a draft, assert ChangeStatusAsync(New) and FollowUpService.AddAsync(statusTo: New) both raise the refusal, the wording is Latin-free, the row is still «مسودة» with OfficialNumber null, no follow-up row was written, and the draft is still deletable by DeleteDraftAsync.

findings.issue: Spec item «FollowUpService … تذكير» is implemented but never runs. IFollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync is complete, idempotent and tested in isolation (A_due_reminder_becomes_one_notification_however_many_times_the_pass_runs, A_reminder_on_a_closed_item_never_rings), but grepping ReminderScheduler.cs for 'Correspondence' or 'followup' returns nothing: no caller exists, so a follow-up reminder instant passes and no bell ever rings in the running product. Carried over from rounds 1 and 2 because ReminderScheduler.cs is outside this package's allowed paths and is concurrently modified by another agent (' M' in the tree).
findings.fix: Not fixable inside b3-corr-services — needs assignment to the ReminderScheduler owner or an explicit grant of that one file. Everything the pass needs is already public: in ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync, resolve IFollowUpService, call RunDueRemindersAsync(now, cancellationToken) alongside the existing meeting/task passes and fold its ReminderRun into the aggregate result. FollowUpService.ReminderKeyKind, ReminderKind and Lookback already match the scheduler's own key convention and window, so no coordination beyond the call is required. Then add one test asserting a due follow-up reminder produces a bell notification through a single ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync.

findings.issue: ExportAsync accepts a caller-supplied request.RecipientPublicKey and seals the container to it with no check that the key belongs to the row's own recipient (`request.RecipientPublicKey ?? await ResolveRecipientKeyAsync(row, ...)`). For an ordinary letter this is a legitimate escape hatch (a party key the caller holds outside the directory), but for a row with RecipientOnly set — AGREEMENT item 7, «لا تُصدَّر إلا إلى النسخة المستلمة» — it means the one flag that restricts distribution is bypassed by a caller parameter.
findings.fix: In ExportAsync, when `row.RecipientOnly` is true, ignore request.RecipientPublicKey and require ResolveRecipientKeyAsync to produce the key from the structure or the party profile; if it cannot, refuse with the existing CoreAr.CorrExchangeNoRecipientKey. Add a test: a recipient-only approved letter whose unit carries no X25519 key is refused even when a valid RecipientPublicKey is passed in the request.

findings.issue: ExchangeMessage carries Confidentiality but not RecipientOnly, so a “للمستلم فقط” letter arrives at the receiving office as an ordinary incoming with the flag cleared, and that office may re-export or sync it onward without ever being told the sender restricted it.
findings.fix: Add `public bool RecipientOnly { get; init; }` to ExchangeMessage (FormatVersion stays 1 — an older reader ignoring an unknown field is the safe direction), set it from row.RecipientOnly in ExportAsync, and pass it through to the CorrespondenceDraftInput built in ImportAsync. Test: export a recipient-only letter and assert the imported incoming carries RecipientOnly and its view's RecipientOnlyAr reads «للمستلم فقط».

findings.issue: Spec asks for «سجل عمليات لكل انتقال» on correspondence; CreateAsync writes an audit row but SetStatusAsync (MarkAnsweredAsync / CloseAsync) writes none, so a referral being answered or closed leaves no trace in the log tab. CreateAsync also accepts a referral on a cancelled or archived correspondence — referring a withdrawn letter to a unit is not an act the office can act on.
findings.fix: In SetStatusAsync, after SaveChangesAsync, call the existing LogAsync with a new CoreAr formatter naming the referral's target and its new Arabic status (reuse CorrespondenceAr.Referral(status)). In CreateAsync, after loading `correspondence`, refuse when its Status is Cancelled or Archived with a plain Arabic sentence. Tests: one asserting an audit row per referral status change, one asserting a referral on a cancelled letter is refused.

findings.issue: RollbackAsync (line ~710) walks `db.ChangeTracker.Entries()` for the WHOLE scoped context, detaching every Added entity and reloading every other tracked one. WakeelDb is scoped to a user session, so a failed registration also discards unsaved in-memory edits belonging to any other screen or service sharing that scope — e.g. a half-typed draft another form is holding, or a Followup queued but not yet saved elsewhere.
findings.fix: Narrow the sweep to the entities this operation touched: capture the correspondence row plus the entries added by duplicates.RecordSuspectedAsync (DuplicateReview) and the official_numbers row, and reload/detach only those — or resolve the sequence-gap problem the comment names by reloading only the OfficialNumberSequence entry and the correspondence row explicitly, leaving the rest of the tracker alone.

findings.issue: Carried over from round 2 and still open: the composed audit summaries CorrAuditRegistered, CorrAuditApproved, CorrAuditCancelled, CorrAuditExported and CorrAuditImported embed a Latin/digit run (an official number like «20260916/12001», a file name) inside an Arabic sentence and are STORED composed, so no screen can wrap the run in <bdi> afterwards and the number can render reordered in a mixed-direction line. This conflicts with the owner's RTL/bidi requirement.
findings.fix: Wrap the embedded run in the Unicode isolate inside the formatter itself, where the composition happens: e.g. `public static string CorrAuditRegistered(string number) => $"سُجّل وارد برقم ⁨{number}⁩";` and the same for CorrAuditApproved, CorrAuditCancelled (the number half), CorrAuditExported (the file name) and CorrAuditImported. Apply the same treatment to the pre-existing Health* strings for consistency, or get the owner's ratification that the audit log is exempt.

Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` (Build succeeded, 0 Warnings, 0 Errors) and `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` (Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 469, Skipped: 0, Total: 469, 27 s). No file was modified, including the progress file.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD (so the builder does not re-litigate it): the numbering discipline is correct — no path writes OfficialNumber outside RegisterIncomingAsync/ApproveOutgoingAsync, both open their own transaction, both call EnsureClockAsync first, both hand the verdict to IOfficialNumberService so the check is not repeated, and RollbackAsync brings the tracked official_numbers row back in step so a failed attempt burns no sequence position. The test for this (A_failure_after_the_number_was_issued_rolls_the_number_back_with_everything_else) is real, not a tautology: it injects a detector that throws inside the transaction after issuance and then asserts the NEXT registration gets 001 and the sequence reads 1. Cancellation keeps the number and stores the reason, and CorrectableFields deliberately excludes OfficialNumber, NumberIssuedAt, ApprovedAt, Direction and Status. CorrectionService's two-pass apply is the right shape for a session-scoped DbContext and is tested by A_batch_that_fails_part_way_writes_nothing_even_after_a_later_save. The Jaccard implementation is correct (union built from left, intersection counted from distinct right; two empty subjects score 0, not 1) and the Arabic duplicate tests exercise diacritics, tatweel and the ة/ه, ى/ي spellings on real subjects. ExchangeService's double-open (probe without chain verification to learn the producer org, then a real open with VerifyCertificateChain only when the org is ours) is the honest way to do item 22, and the three distinct signature sentences say exactly what was proven. Every user-facing string in the package is Arabic with no technical term and no error code; CorrespondenceRefusedException carries the finished sentence plus per-field issues. Migrations 0003/0004 are well-reasoned and the per-direction unique index is the right call.

VERDICT RATIONALE: 'fix' rests on finding 1, which is inside the package's allowed paths and is the same class of bug round 2 fixed elsewhere — a draft reaching «جديد» with no number through ChangeStatusAsync or FollowUpService.AddAsync produces a row that can no longer be deleted, cancelled or corrected while still being counted by the attention center and the badge. Roughly ten lines plus one CoreAr string and two tests. Finding 2 is also medium but cannot be fixed here; it needs an owner decision on granting ReminderScheduler.cs or reassigning that one call.

The builder's four open_issues from round 2 were re-checked: the ReminderScheduler gap is real (confirmed by grep — no correspondence pass exists) and is listed above; the soft-delete reading of item 19 is defensible and user-visibly identical (global query filter, no restore command) but still wants the owner's ratification; the DATA-MODEL §0 line about the global unique index is genuinely stale against Migration 0003 and belongs to the schema/docs owner; the bidi-isolate question is restated here as a low finding with the concrete formatter change, since it is cheap to apply inside CoreAr and does not need a screen.
